skill.name: firecrawl-web
skill.description: Adds Firecrawl-backed web scraping, screenshots, structured extraction, search, and documentation crawling for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
skill.summary: Use Firecrawl to fetch pages, screenshots, search results, extracted fields, and crawled documentation.
skill.author: BexTuychiev

security_audit.summary: The skill performs legitimate Firecrawl web access, so many documentation-only command examples, code fences, and placeholder URLs are false positives. Confirmed risks include third-party page and screenshot processing, home .env loading, credential setup in ~/.env, and user-directed file writes. No prompt injection or malicious override text was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Third-party processing of URLs and page content
remediation.suggestion: Document that URLs, search queries, extraction prompts, schemas, page content, and screenshots are sent to Firecrawl.

remediation.issue: Screenshot capture can expose sensitive pages
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before screenshots of private, authenticated, or sensitive pages.

remediation.issue: Home dotenv loading broadens secret exposure
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a skill-scoped config file or FIRECRAWL_API_KEY from the current environment instead of loading ~/.env.

remediation.issue: User-controlled output paths can overwrite files
remediation.suggestion: Resolve outputs under the workspace, reject parent traversal, and warn before replacing existing files.

remediation.issue: Crawl commands can consume credits or scrape too broadly
remediation.suggestion: Set a conservative maximum crawl limit and require confirmation before large crawls.

finding_verdicts.reason: This is a .gitignore entry that prevents committing .env files. It is not code that reads or writes environment secrets.
urllib.request is imported for the screenshot download path used later in the script. This creates intentional external network access for remote screenshot assets.
urlretrieve downloads a Firecrawl-provided screenshot URL to a local output path. This is expected functionality, but it pulls remote content into the workspace.
The screenshot command writes decoded image bytes to a user-controlled output_path. Without path restrictions or overwrite checks, it can overwrite local files.
The crawl command writes markdown files under a user-provided output directory. It can create or overwrite files without an explicit overwrite guard.
The dotenv library is used by this script to load API credentials. This is expected, but it introduces process-level secret handling.
load_dotenv() imports variables from a local .env file into the process. Local dotenv loading can expose secrets to dependencies used by the script.
The script loads Path.home() / .env, which may contain secrets for unrelated projects. Loading the home dotenv file broadens secret exposure.
The imported dotenv loader is later used to load API credentials. This is legitimate setup code, but it is still environment secret access.
The script loads a local dotenv file before running commands. That can bring sensitive variables into a network-capable process.
The script explicitly loads the user home .env file. This may import secrets beyond the Firecrawl API key into the process.
The base64 decode handles Firecrawl screenshot image data before writing a PNG. The decoded bytes are not executed or interpreted as code.

semantic_findings.title: Third-Party Firecrawl Data Transfer
semantic_findings.description: The skill routes user URLs, searches, extraction prompts, crawl targets, and screenshot requests through Firecrawl. This can expose sensitive page targets or content to an external service.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The README states the skill uses Firecrawl, and fc.py calls Firecrawl scrape, search, and crawl APIs with user-supplied targets and prompts.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted Web Crawling Targets
semantic_findings.description: The command parsers accept arbitrary URLs for markdown, screenshot, extraction, and crawl operations without domain allowlists. This can enable unintended scraping or broad crawling when prompts are imprecise.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The argparse definitions expose URL inputs for each network command, and the skill documentation only warns about credits rather than target restrictions.

content.value_statement: Teams need current page content, screenshots, and structured web data inside AI coding workflows. This skill connects Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to Firecrawl web tools.
actual_capabilities: Fetch a webpage as markdown using the markdown command.
Capture full-page screenshots and save them as PNG files.
Extract structured data from a page using a JSON schema.
Search the web through Firecrawl and print titles, URLs, and descriptions.
Crawl documentation sites and save page markdown files.
limitations: Requires a valid Firecrawl API key and Firecrawl account credits.
Sends requested URLs and content processing requests to Firecrawl.
Does not enforce domain allowlists or private URL detection.
Output paths depend on user input and can overwrite local files.

use_cases.title: Research Current Documentation
use_cases.description: Fetch and crawl framework documentation before answering setup or API questions.

use_cases.title: Capture Visual Page State
use_cases.description: Take a full-page screenshot for review, bug reports, or design comparison.

use_cases.title: Collect Product Page Fields
use_cases.description: Extract selected fields from public product pages using a defined schema.

prompt_templates.title: Fetch Page Markdown
prompt_templates.prompt: Use firecrawl-web to get markdown from <URL> and summarize the main content.

prompt_templates.title: Capture a Screenshot
prompt_templates.prompt: Use firecrawl-web to take a full-page screenshot of <URL> and save it as page.png.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Structured Fields
prompt_templates.prompt: Use firecrawl-web to extract title, price, and feature list from <URL> with a schema.

prompt_templates.title: Crawl Documentation Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Use firecrawl-web to crawl <DOCS_URL> with a limit of 20 pages, then identify setup steps and API examples.

output_examples.input: Fetch markdown from a library release notes page.
output_examples.output: Clean markdown content with headings, links, and the main article text.

output_examples.input: Take a screenshot of a product page.
output_examples.output: A saved PNG file path and a short confirmation message.

output_examples.input: Crawl a documentation site with a small limit.
output: Page summaries saved as markdown files.
A list of titles and key installation notes.

best_practices: Use only public URLs unless the user confirms private data can be sent to Firecrawl.
Set small crawl limits before expanding a crawl.
Save screenshots and crawl output inside the current project folder.
anti_patterns: Do not crawl large sites without a clear limit.
Do not use the skill for pages that contain private credentials or personal data.
Do not save output to home, system, or shared configuration directories.

faq.question: Does this skill require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires a Firecrawl API key available in the environment or dotenv configuration.

faq.question: Can it browse any website?
faq.answer: It can request public URLs through Firecrawl, subject to Firecrawl limits and website access rules.

faq.question: Does it send data to an external service?
faq.answer: Yes. URLs, search queries, extraction prompts, and screenshot requests are sent to Firecrawl.

faq.question: Can it save files locally?
faq.answer: Yes. Screenshot and crawl commands can save files to paths chosen in the command.

faq.question: Is it suitable for private pages?
faq.answer: Use caution. Private URLs or page content may be processed by Firecrawl.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
